claim: Functional specs serve two audiences: humans and AI coding agents, which have different formatting needs
quote: Use Clear Structure (Headings & Lists) to help AI understand requirements. Breaking content into logical sections, bullet points, and tables creates a roadmap that language models can parse effectively.

claim: Optimising specs for only one audience breaks the other; six structural areas are essential for AI-readable specs
quote: Clarity is king. Many devs use Markdown headings or XML-like tags in the spec to delineate sections, because AI models handle well-structured text better than free-form prose.

claim: Keeborg generates both human-readable and agent-optimised spec layers (including CLAUDE.md and .cursorrules) in 90 seconds
quote: Keeborg generates 8 interconnected specification documents in under 90 seconds. Produces agent-optimized formats with CLAUDE.md and .cursorrules files.

claim: Kiro is an AWS agentic IDE that forces review of the machine-readable spec layer before any code executes
quote: Kiro operates at the specification layer first. Before writing a single line of code, Kiro helps you formalize your intent into a structured spec.

claim: Purpose-built PM agents retain organisational memory; generic chatbots start fresh every session
quote: Purpose-built PM agents retain organizational memory, while generic chatbots 'start fresh with every conversation,' creating friction through constant context re-explanation.

claim: AI enhances requirements management via NLP/ML/LLM; human review is structurally required in regulated industries
quote: Human review isn't optional here. It's a structural requirement baked into every applicable standard in safety-critical industries.

claim: aqua converts voice notes into structured requirements in 15 seconds; top 5 AI tools for requirements management 2026
quote: Creating requirements with your voice and AI is a major time saver — generate complete requirements in 15 seconds.

claim: Copilot4DevOps generates FRDs, PRDs, and solution design documents natively inside Azure DevOps
quote: Business analysts and other team members can use it to generate functional/non-functional requirements documents, PRDs, and solution design documents.

claim: Kiro generates EARS-structured requirements by default; launched internationally May 2026 as AWS's answer to structureless agentic coding
quote: Kiro uses EARS notation with formal logic to catch contradictions before code generation. Amazon launched Kiro internationally on May 7, 2026 — not as a feature update, but as a ground-up replacement for Amazon Q Developer.

claim: SDD has three maturity levels (spec-first, spec-anchored, spec-as-source); Kiro, Spec Kit, and Tessl each target different levels
quote: Spec-first: Specs precede coding but may be discarded afterward. Spec-anchored: Specs persist for ongoing feature evolution. Spec-as-source: Specs become primary artifacts; humans edit only specs, never code.

claim: Six best spec-driven development tools for AI coding in 2026: Augment Cosmos, Amazon Kiro, GitHub Spec Kit, OpenSpec, BMAD-METHOD, Cursor
quote: The most important decision factor: living vs. static specifications. Living specs automatically synchronize with implementation; static specs require manual updates, creating drift within hours.

claim: EARS notation developed at Rolls-Royce; adopted by Airbus, Bosch, NASA, Siemens; reduces ambiguity in requirements
quote: Organizations using EARS include blue chip companies such as Airbus, Bosch, Dyson, Honeywell, Intel, NASA, Rolls-Royce and Siemens.

claim: EARS requirements are consistent across different authors, making AI-generated drafts easier to validate
quote: EARS requirements are simpler and more consistent, even if written by different authors, and the simplicity means they are universally understandable.

claim: Inflectra.ai scores existing requirements against EARS framework using Amazon Nova LLMs and suggests improvements
quote: Allows Business Analysts, product owners and quality assurance managers to review requirements against the EARS framework using Generative AI and Amazon Nova family of LLMs.

claim: SDD fails the same way BDD failed: when only one role owns spec files they become abandoned documentation
quote: QA engineers wrote .feature files alone, product managers rarely reviewed them, developers treated them as 'QA stuff.' This same trap threatens SDD if only testers write specifications for testing purposes alone.

claim: Effective BA prompts follow Role + Context + Task + Constraints + Output format; 32-prompt toolkit across functional requirements, data mapping, and test cases
quote: All prompts follow a consistent structure: role definition, context provision, specific task, and expected output format — designed for compatibility with Claude, ChatGPT, or Copilot.

claim: Jira Rovo AI drafts acceptance criteria from Confluence docs and flags gaps in user stories
quote: Rovo, Atlassian's AI assistant built into Jira, draws directly on Confluence documentation to clarify user stories and expand acceptance criteria by bringing in relevant business rules.

claim: Copilot4DevOps Elicit feature generates user stories with acceptance criteria and test cases from parent work items in Azure Boards
quote: The 'Elicit' feature of Copilot4DevOps can generate user stories with test cases, acceptance criteria, pseudocode, etc., based on the parent work item's content.

claim: AI documentation changed from assisted writing to autonomous agents; 85-90% reductions in content creation time with 340% coverage increase
quote: Teams report 85–90% reductions in content creation time while increasing coverage by 340%. Notion's AI agents work autonomously for up to 20 minutes, processing hundreds of pages.

claim: AI generates Gherkin scenarios in under a minute but misses business intent and edge cases; treat as coverage scaffold
quote: AI can write syntactically valid Gherkin quickly, but it frequently produces scenarios that miss the actual business intent or skip non-functional requirements like performance and security.

claim: BA role shifts from writing specs to validating and refining AI-generated specs — more architectural, less clerical
quote: By 2026, the role of a Business Analyst has undergone a fundamental shift. Rather than functioning as a 'data gatherer,' the modern BA operates as a Strategic Value Designer.
